title: Structural, roof and facade warning signs
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: SafeWork NSW, Work on roofs code of practice (document dated May 2026; commenced 22 May 2026); WorkSafe Victoria, High risk work licence (reviewed 30 June 2026); SafeWork NSW, High risk work licences (last modified 15 June 2026); WorkSafe Queensland, Boom type elevating work platform (WP) (no date shown); Consumer Affairs Victoria, What work requires a building contract? (last updated 25 September 2025).
audience: Property manager partner workers who inspect buildings from ground level and must recognise structural or exterior warning signs
learningOutcomes: Recognise warning signs of structural movement, roof failure and facade deterioration from ground level.
Decide what can be recorded from safe ground-level positions and what must not be done.
Refer structural, roof and facade concerns to licensed or competent persons, and record the referral.

instruction.heading: Warning signs from ground level
instruction.body: Structural problems often show as change over time. Look for cracks that are wider than a hairline, cracks that have grown since an earlier record, doors and windows that have started to stick in a new way, floors that slope, and gaps opening at junctions between walls and ceilings. On the roof and facade, look for loose or missing tiles and sheeting, sagging gutters or roof lines, rusted or loose fixings, crumbling or spalling concrete and render, and balustrades or handrails that move. Record each sign from a safe position, with photographs taken from the ground where possible and with consent.

instruction.heading: What not to do
instruction.body: Do not climb onto a roof, a ladder or a platform to inspect a warning sign unless the access is authorised, safe and within the worker's training and equipment. Do not push, lean on, or test a balustrade, wall or structure to see how it moves. Do not remove finishes or cover cracks to see what is behind them. Keep people clear of the area below any loose item, and control access as set out in “Risk prioritisation and escalation”.

instruction.heading: Refer and record
instruction.body: Structural, roof and facade concerns are referred to a licensed building trade or to a competent specialist, as the site requires. Record the sign, its change over time if known, the protection in place, and the referral. Do not say the building is structurally sound or that the roof is watertight. A referral that says what was seen and what was not inspected is more useful to the owner than a reassuring statement that cannot be supported.

procedure: Inspect from a safe ground-level position and record each sign with location, time and any change from earlier records.
Do not climb, lean on, push or test any structure, balustrade or roof item.
Keep people clear of any loose item and control access where needed.
Refer roof, facade and structural concerns to the licensed or competent person.
Record the referral, the protection in place and the owner of the next action.
Do not describe the structure or roof as sound unless a competent person has confirmed it.

workedExamples.situation: A wide crack has appeared above a door since the last inspection, and a gutter at the front of the building sags near a loose fixing.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the inspection record, and what should not be said to the owner?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record both signs from the ground, note the crack has changed since the last record, and mark the loose gutter fixing as a falling-object hazard with access controlled below. Refer the crack and the roof item to a licensed building trade or competent specialist. Do not say the building is structurally sound, because the inspection cannot establish that.

equipmentAndPpe: Torch and tape measure for recording crack widths from the ground
Camera or phone for photographs from the ground, with consent
Barrier tape or cones for keeping people clear below

commonErrors.error: Climbing onto a roof to look at a loose tile or gutter.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect from the ground, control access below, and refer.

commonErrors.error: Covering a crack with filler to make the wall look sound.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the crack and refer it. Do not cover the sign.

commonErrors.error: Telling the owner the building is structurally sound after a visual check.
commonErrors.prevention: State only what was seen and what was not inspected.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Roof work: SafeWork NSW's code for work on roofs (document dated May 2026, in force from 22 May 2026) covers commercial and industrial roofs and does not extend to residential roofs.

Height access: a boom-type elevating work platform needs the WP licence in Victoria, with no boom-length threshold (WorkSafe Victoria page, reviewed 30 June 2026). In New South Wales and Queensland the licence applies at a boom of 11 metres or more, so a shorter boom may not need it there (SafeWork NSW licence page; WorkSafe Queensland page). This lesson does not grant a licence. In Victoria, scissor lifts sit outside the WP requirement (WorkSafe Victoria page, reviewed 30 June 2026).

Structural work: the Consumer Affairs Victoria page (last updated 25 September 2025) ties builder registration to re-blocking and re-stumping, and to demolition and removal of a home, without a dollar threshold for those items. Refer structural work to a registered licensed trade.
Completing this lesson does not give a building, roofing, structural or height-work licence, certificate or authority.

qualityStandard: Every sign is recorded from a safe position with location and time.
No structure, roof item or balustrade is climbed, leaned on or tested.
Every concern is referred and no structure is described as sound without competent confirmation.
documentationEvidence: Ground-level observation record with photographs taken with consent
Crack or movement record compared with any earlier record
Referral note with the protection in place and the next owner
summary: Look for change over time: cracks, sticking doors, sagging lines and loose fixings.
Observe from the ground, do not climb or test, and control access below.
Refer, record and never describe a structure as sound without competent confirmation.

knowledgeChecks.question: A roof tile looks loose. What is the correct response for a property manager partner worker?
options: Inspect from the ground, control access below, and refer to a competent roofing trade
Climb onto the roof to fix it, since the tile will be quick to secure in place
Push the tile back into place and tap it down with the palm of the hand to hold it
Cover the tile with sealant from the ground, so that water can no longer reach the roof

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement is correct after a visual inspection of a building's structure?
options: The building is structurally sound, so no further checks are needed
Only what was seen and what was not inspected can be stated
The roof is watertight, since no leaks were seen on the day
The structure is compliant with the standards that apply to it

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the lesson say about testing a structure to see how it moves?
options: Push or lean on it to see how it moves
Do not push, lean on, or test it to see how it moves
Test it from the roof first
Cover the cracks, then test it
